summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish the DisabilityCare Australia Fund to hold revenue from the proposed Medicare levy increase and reimburse governments for disability scheme expenditure.
The Treasurer would determine credits based on tax office revenue advice, and the Future Fund Board would invest the money under ministerial directions.
State and territory reimbursements would require written agreements, while a separate transitional account would support the National Disability Insurance Scheme's initial implementation.
changes: The state and territory allocation would start at $825 million in 2014-15 and rise by 3.5 per cent annually until 2023-24.
Investment and administration expenses would be paid from fund earnings rather than levy proceeds.
Ministers could not direct investment in a particular financial asset or support for a particular business.
Fund arrangements would require review before 30 June 2024 unless responsible Ministers agreed to a later date.
summary.affected: The Commonwealth, state and territory governments, responsible Ministers and the Future Fund Board of Guardians are affected.

speeches.speaker: Wayne Swan
speeches.brief: Moved the DisabilityCare Australia Fund Bill, proposing that increased Medicare levy revenue be paid into a dedicated fund managed by the Future Fund Board of Guardians and used to support DisabilityCare Australia and reimburse states and territories for eligible scheme costs.

speeches.speaker: David Bradbury
speeches.brief: Summing up debate on the DisabilityCare Australia funding bills, confirmed the Medicare levy will rise from 1½ per cent to two per cent from 1 July 2014, with about $9.7 billion of the extra revenue allocated to states and territories over 10 years, and explained the Future Fund Board of Guardians will manage the new DisabilityCare Australia Fund covering 410,000 Australians with disability.
